newsitem.title: EGYPT: MOODY'S SAYS OUTLOOK FOR EGYPT IMPROVING.
newsitem.headline: MOODY'S SAYS OUTLOOK FOR EGYPT IMPROVING.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday that its outlook for Egypt's sovereign rating was improving because the Cairo government was consolidating the pace and content of structural reform in the country.

The international rating agency, which assigned Egypt a BA2 sovereign ceiling rating in October, said privatisation, a good budget performance and a declining rate of inflation were among the factors that had helped bolster Egypt's outlook.

"The privatisation programme, which is a key element in Egypt's effort to revitalise its real economy, has remained at the forefront of the policy agenda," Moody's said in a statement sent to Reuters.

"Although actual privatisations have not matched the government's highly ambitious schedule, and are likely to continue to fall behind official targets, what has been achieved since 1996 is still noteworthy, given the previous slow progress in this area," it added.
Egypt's economic reform programme has focused on dismantling its large public sector through share offers, and on liberalising trade and attracting foreign investors.
"Egypt's solid budget performance, declining inflation rate and the low and moderating foreign currency debt burden further bolster the improved outlook," Moody's said.
According to government statistics, Egypt's year-on-year inflation fell to 4.8 percent in June, its lowest level in more than six years, from 4.9 percent in May and 8.3 percent in June 1996.
Egypt's debt burden decreased last year when the Paris Club agreed to write off about $4 billion of debt, the third and last tranche of debt covered by an agreement dating back to 1991.
The agreement to waive the last tranche had been conditional on International Monetary Fund approval of the Egyptian government's economic reform programme.
But Moody's was less enthusiastic about what it said were Egypt's "low domestic saving and weak non-oil exports" which it said put a damper on the country's long-term economic prospects.
